title: The Inspector's Lost Casefile
description: We recovered an old casefile from a damaged terminal. Opening casefile.txt shows corrupted gibberish starting with PK... Inspect the clues, uncover the real file format, and extract the secret flag!
author: J Daniel Wonderson

title: The Quantum Gateway
description:
We managed to intercept the local login portal for the Quantum Gateway, but the system is locked down and waiting for an initialization sequence.

The original developers were known for leaving maintenance notes in their code and hiding access PINs directly in the system's architecture. You will need to look "under the hood," manipulate the browser's memory, and trigger a manual boot sequence to retrieve the flag.
author: J Daniel Wonderson

title: The Phantom Dump
description:
A rogue agent wiped the central database, but we managed to pull a single raw system diagnostic log before the server died. We know they hid their master access key inside the traffic noise.

You'll need to parse the data, follow the breadcrumbs, and peel back multiple layers of encryption to find the flag.
author: J Daniel Wonderson

title: The Obsidian Canvas
description:
An unknown artist sent us this digital canvas. When we open it, it's just a blank, dark void. But in cybersecurity, what you see isn't always what you get. Images are just math and code rendered by a machine.

You'll need to manipulate the fabric of the image itself to shed some light on the situation. Once you can see the payload, you'll have to decipher the artist's sequence to extract the flag.
author: J Daniel Wonderson

title: The Intercepted Drop
description:
We intercepted a communication between two unknown operatives. We know they are planning a drop-off at a major global monument, but standard email software isn't showing us the whole picture.

Examine the raw transmission, peel back the layers of the custom headers, and track down the geographic coordinates of the dropzone.
author: J Daniel Wonderson

title: The Fragmented Network
description:
Our primary database went down in a targeted attack. The system attempted an emergency backup, but the fail-safe shattered the master key across multiple global server nodes to prevent the attackers from stealing it.

We managed to download the network_config.json file. You need to read the system's recovery protocol, filter out the decoy nodes, and reassemble the master key to capture the flag.
author: J Daniel Wonderson
